record.title: Eventual tail conjecture for four-stack Twyst-off positions
record.statement:
Consider positions in Twyst-off with four stacks, written $(a,b,c,a)$, and let a **$P$ position** be one from which the next player has no winning move.

**Eventual tail conjecture.** For every $a>0$, there exist integers $c_0>b_0>a$ such that

$$
(a,b_0,c,a)\text{ is a }P\text{ position if and only if }c\geq c_0.
$$

This predicts an eventual interval of $P$ positions as the third stack grows, for a suitable fixed second stack. The statement appears after observations that remaining four-stack $P$ positions are complicated but exhibit long-run patterns; no proof or resolution is supplied.
record.source_name: Alex Meadows and Brad Putman, “A New Twist on Wythoff's Game”, arXiv:1606.06819 (2016).

record.title: The classification conjecture for ten-vertex graphs with lazy cop number three
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph on 10 vertices, let $R_3=K_3\square K_3$ be the $3\times3$ Rooks graph, and let $c_L(G)$ denote its lazy cop number.

**Ten-vertex classification conjecture.** The only graphs $G$ on 10 vertices with $c_L(G)=3$ are either the Petersen graph, or a copy of $R_3$ with an additional vertex $v$ whose degree is at most 5 and whose adjacencies are chosen in a particular way so as not to reduce the lazy cop number to two.

The conjecture is intended to characterize the graphs needed for the paper's proposed analysis of graphs with maximum degree four. The source describes the required adjacency conditions only qualitatively, and reports no proof or resolution.
record.source_name: Brendan W. Sullivan, Nikolas Townsend and Mikayla Werzanski, “The 3x3 rooks graph is the unique smallest graph with lazy cop number 3”, arXiv:1606.08485 (2016).

record.title: The tournament Erdős–Hajnal conjecture
record.statement:
A **tournament** is a directed graph in which exactly one of $uv$ and $vu$ is an edge for every pair of distinct vertices. A tournament $T$ is **$S$-free** if it has no subtournament isomorphic to $S$. Let $\alpha(T)$ be the maximum number of vertices in a transitive subtournament of $T$.

**Tournament Erdős–Hajnal conjecture.** For every tournament $S$, there exists a constant $\delta(S)>0$ such that every $S$-free tournament $T$ satisfies

$$
\alpha(T)\geq |V(T)|^{\delta(H)}.
$$

The source states this as equivalent to the graph Erdős–Hajnal conjecture. Transitive subtournaments provide a single analogue of cliques and stable sets, but the conjecture remains open in general; the exponent in the source is written as $\delta(H)$ despite the quantified tournament being $S$.
record.source_name: Maria Chudnovsky, “The Erdös-Hajnal Conjecture—A Survey”, arXiv:1606.08827 (2016).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1606.08827

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of June 2016). “In fact, what is really proved in is the following: Every bull-free graph is $2$-narrow.”

record.title: Plancherel dimension-ratio decay conjecture for subpartitions
record.statement:
Let $\lambda\vdash n$. Write $\mu\subseteq\lambda$ when $\mu$ is a partition obtained from $\lambda$ by removing boxes, and let $P_{PL}^n$ denote Plancherel measure on partitions of $n$. For a nonnegative integer $s$, consider subpartitions of size $|\lambda|-s$.

**Plancherel dimension-ratio decay conjecture.** There exists $\alpha>0$ such that, for all $s$,

$$
P_{PL}^n\left(\left\{\lambda:\max_{\substack{\mu\colon\mu\subseteq\lambda\\|\mu|=|\lambda|-s}}\frac{\dim\mu}{\dim\lambda}>n^{-\alpha s}\right\}\right)\to 0.
$$

This conjecture asserts polynomial decay of the largest dimension ratio after removing $s$ boxes, with probability tending to one under Plancherel measure. The paper presents this as an open estimate needed to control contributions from smaller partitions.
record.source_name: Dario De Stavola, “Partial sum of matrix entries of representations of the symmetric group and its asymptotics”, arXiv:1606.09158 (2017).

record.title: Eventual crossing-free-edge conjecture for extremal subgraphs of $D_n$
record.statement: Let $D_n$ be the graph under consideration, let $e_\ell(n)$ denote the maximum number of edges in a subgraph of $D_n$ with local crossing number $\ell$, and call an edge **crossing free** if it is crossed zero times. **Eventual crossing-free-edge conjecture.** For each integer $\ell\geq 0$ there is a positive integer $N_\ell$ such that for all integers $n\geq N_\ell$ there is a subgraph $G$ of $D_n$ with local crossing number $\ell$ such that $G$ has a crossing free edge and $e(G)=e_\ell(n)$. The claim would provide optimal constructions that are parallel compositions of smaller graphs for fixed $\ell$ and sufficiently large $n$; the paper gives no resolution in the supplied context.

record.title: Özkahya–Young anti-Ramsey matching conjecture
record.statement:
Let $ar(n,k,s)$ be the least number of nonempty color classes in a coloring (partition) of ${[n]\choose k}$ that guarantees a rainbow $s$-matching, meaning $s$ pairwise disjoint $k$-sets belonging to pairwise distinct color classes. Let $e_k(n,s-1)$ denote the maximum size of a $k$-uniform family in $[n]$ with matching number less than $s-1$. **Özkahya–Young anti-Ramsey matching conjecture.** For all $n>sk$,

$$
ar(n,k,s)=e_k(n,s-1)+2.
$$
 This conjecture connects anti-Ramsey numbers with extremal matching problems; the supplied source gives no resolution or partial-result status.
record.source_name: Peter Frankl and Andrey Kupavskii, “Two problems on matchings in set families - in the footsteps of Erdős and Kleitman”, arXiv:1607.06126 (2018).

record.title: Maximal-denominator conjecture for semiqueens
record.statement: Let $\mathbb Q^{21}$ be the semiqueen, and let $F_m$ denote the $m$th Fibonacci number. **Semiqueen maximal-denominator conjecture.** The largest denominator of a vertex configuration for $q$ semiqueens is $F_{\lfloor q/2\rfloor}$ when $q$ is even, and $F_{\lfloor q/2\rfloor+1}-1$ when $q$ is odd. The paper exhibits the relevant golden-parallelogram configurations, but the maximality claim remains open.
record.source_name: Seth Chaiken, Christopher R. H. Hanusa and Thomas Zaslavsky, “A q-Queens Problem. V. Some of Our Favorite Pieces: Queens, Bishops, Rooks, and Nightriders”, arXiv:1609.00853 (2020).

record.title: Maximal-denominator conjecture for frontal queens
record.statement: Let $\mathbb Q^{12}$ be the frontal queen, and let $F_m$ denote the $m$th Fibonacci number. **Frontal-queen maximal-denominator conjecture.** The largest denominator of a vertex configuration for $q$ frontal queens is $2F_{q/2}-1$ when $q$ is even, and $F_{(q+3)/2}-1$ when $q$ is odd. The paper derives these values for the displayed configurations, but does not prove that no other configuration has a larger denominator.

record.title: Conjecture on the cop number of fast robbers on grids
record.statement:
For $R\in\mathbb{N}$, let $f_R(n)$ be the minimum number of cops needed to catch a robber of speed $R$ on an $n\times n$ grid, where the cops move at unit speed. Here “sufficiently large” refers to the robber speed parameter $R$.

**Fast-robber grid conjecture.** For all sufficiently large $R\in\mathbb{N}$,

$$
f_R(n)=n^{1-o(1)}\quad\text{as }n\to\infty.
$$

The conjecture says that, for sufficiently large fixed robber speeds, the trivial upper bound $f_R(n)\le n$ is asymptotically close to the truth. The paper proves a much weaker exponential lower bound for one sufficiently large speed and leaves this near-linear behaviour conjectural.
record.source_name: Paul Balister, Béla Bollobás, Bhargav Narayanan and Amy Shaw, “Catching a fast robber on the grid”, arXiv:1609.01002 (2017).

record.title: Erdős–Faudree–Sós conjecture on size pairs of induced subgraphs of Ramsey graphs
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph on $n$ vertices. For a graph $H$, write $v(H)$ and $e(H)$ for its numbers of vertices and edges, and define

$$
\Psi(G)=\{(v(H),e(H)): H \text{ is an induced subgraph of }G\}.
$$

For $C>0$, let $G$ be **$C$-Ramsey** if its largest homogeneous set has size at most $C\log n$.

**Erdős–Faudree–Sós conjecture.** For any $C>0$, there exists a $\delta=\delta(C)>0$ such that

$$
|\Psi(G)|\ge \delta n^{5/2}
$$

for every $C$-Ramsey graph $G$ on $n$ vertices.

The conjecture asserts that Ramsey graphs have many distinct vertex-count and edge-count pairs among their induced subgraphs, in analogy with dense random graphs. Its status is not specified in the source.
record.source_name: Bhargav Narayanan, Julian Sahasrabudhe and István Tomon, “Ramsey graphs induce subgraphs of many different sizes”, arXiv:1609.01705 (2017).

record.title: Optimal dimension reduction bound for Euclidean point sets
record.statement:
Let $f(n,d,\varepsilon)$ denote the smallest $m$ such that every $n$-point subset of $\ell_2^d$ can be embedded into $\ell_2^m$ with distortion at most $1+\varepsilon$. **Dimension-reduction conjecture.** For all $n,d>1$ and $0<\varepsilon<1$, 

$$
f(n,d,\varepsilon)=\Theta\left(\min\left\{n,d,\varepsilon^{-2}\lg(2+\varepsilon^2n)\right\}\right).
$$
 This conjecture predicts the optimal Euclidean target dimension across the full range of distortion parameters, including the regime where $\varepsilon$ approaches $1/\sqrt{\min\{n,d\}}$; the paper proves a matching lower bound up to a logarithmic factor in a nearly full range of $\varepsilon$, while the stated formula remains the conjectural optimal form.

record.title: Conjecture that the compatibility density of delta-matroids tends to zero
record.statement:
For each $n\geq 2$, let $\Gamma_n$ be the proportion defined in the paper for compatible pairs of labelled delta-matroids. The sequence $(\Gamma_n)_{n\geq 2}$ is decreasing and bounded below by zero, so its limit exists. **Compatibility-density conjecture.**

$$
\Gamma_n \to 0 \quad \text{as } n \to \infty.
$$

The conjecture is motivated by the observed values $\Gamma_2=1$, $\Gamma_3 \simeq 0.865$, $\Gamma_4 \simeq 0.649$, $\Gamma_5 \simeq 0.476$, and $\Gamma_6 \simeq 0.369$, together with the authors' inability to find larger classes of delta-matroids than those used for their lower bound. No resolution is given in the source.
record.source_name: Daryl Funk, Dillon Mayhew and Steven D. Noble, “How many delta-matroids are there?”, arXiv:1609.08244 (2017).

record.title: The homomorphism threshold conjecture for odd-cycle-free graphs
record.statement:
Let $\ell \ge 4$ be an integer. For a family of graphs $\mathcal{H}$, the **homomorphism threshold** $\delta_{\hom}(\mathcal{H})$ is the infimum of $d$ such that every $\mathcal{H}$-free graph with $n$ vertices and minimum degree at least $dn$ is homomorphic to an $\mathcal{H}$-free graph of bounded order. In this setting, $\mathcal{H}={C_3,C_5,\ldots,C_{2\ell-1}}$.

**Homomorphism threshold conjecture.**

$$
\delta_{\hom}({C_3, C_5 \ldots, C_{2\ell-1}}) = \frac{1}{2\ell-1}.
$$

The preceding construction shows that, for even $\ell$, the stronger proposed homomorphism conclusion to one of the graphs $F_k^\ell$ fails, while the corresponding extension for odd $\ell$ remains open. This conjecture concerns the homomorphism threshold itself for all integers $\ell \ge 4$.
record.source_name: Shoham Letzter and Richard Snyder, “The homomorphism threshold of \C_3, C_5\-free graphs”, arXiv:1610.04932 (2018).

record.title: Conjecture A on decomposition numbers of defect-two characters
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite group, let $p$ be a prime, and let $\chi\in\operatorname{Irr}(G)$ satisfy

$$
|G|_p=p^2\cdot\chi(1)_p.
$$

Here $n_p$ denotes the largest power of $p$ dividing the integer $n$, $\operatorname{IBr}(G)$ is a set of irreducible $p$-Brauer characters of $G$, $\chi^0$ is the restriction of $\chi$ to the elements of $G$ of order prime to $p$, and

$$
\operatorname{IBr}(\chi^0)=\{\varphi\in\operatorname{IBr}(G)\mid d_{\chi\varphi}\ne0\}.
$$

**Conjecture A.** One has $|\operatorname{IBr}(\chi^0)|\le p^2-1$ and $d_{\chi\varphi}\le p$ for every $\varphi\in\operatorname{IBr}(G)$.
record.source_name: Gunter Malle, Gabriel Navarro and Benjamin Sambale, “On defects of characters and decomposition numbers”, arXiv:1611.01284 (2016).

record.title: The bounded-degree tree Ramsey goodness conjecture
record.statement:
Let $T$ be a tree, let $\Delta$ and $k$ be positive integers, and let $H$ be a graph with chromatic number $\chi(H)=k$. A graph $T$ is **$H$-good** if its Ramsey number with $H$ satisfies $r(T,H)=|T|+|H|-2$. **Bounded-degree tree Ramsey goodness conjecture.** For all $\Delta$ and $k$ there exists a constant $C_{\Delta,k}$ such that, for any tree $T$ with maximum degree at most $\Delta$ and any graph $H$ with $\chi(H)=k$ satisfying

$$
|T|\geq C_{\Delta,k}|H|,
$$

$T$ is $H$-good. The paper establishes the corresponding range up to logarithmic factors; the conjecture asserts that these factors can be removed.
record.source_name: Igor Balla, Alexey Pokrovskiy and Benny Sudakov, “Ramsey goodness of bounded degree trees”, arXiv:1611.02688 (2016).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1611.02688

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2016).

record.title: Awanless–Barát rainbow matching conjecture
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a bipartite graph and let $E_1,\ldots,E_m$ be sets of edges. Write $\Delta(H)$ for the maximum degree of a graph $H$. A **rainbow matching** is a matching containing an edge from every set $E_i$. **Awanless–Barát rainbow matching conjecture.** If

$$
|E_i|>\Delta\left(\bigcup_{i\leqslant m}E_i\right)+1
$$

for every $i$, then there exists a rainbow matching.

The paper records this as a related conjecture and gives an example showing that the corresponding bound with $+1$ replacing $+2$ does not suffice; it also notes failure for multisets. The stated conjecture remains open in the source.
record.source_name: Ron Aharoni, Noga Alon, Eli Berger, Maria Chudnovsky, Dani Kotlar, Martin Loebl and Ran Ziv, “Fair representation by independent sets”, arXiv:1611.03196 (2016).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1611.03196

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of November 2016). “This is proved in if $s$ is any power of $2$.”

record.title: Fair matching conjecture for graph edge partitions
record.statement:
Let $H$ be a graph with maximum degree $\Delta(H)$, and partition its edge set into $E_1,\ldots,E_m$. A **matching** is a set of pairwise vertex-disjoint edges. **Fair matching conjecture.** There exists a matching $M$ such that

$$
|M\cap E_i|\geqslant \left\lfloor\frac{|E_i|}{\Delta(H)+2}\right\rfloor\quad\text{for all }i\leqslant m.
$$

The paper describes this as an even stronger version of the preceding matching conjectures and gives no resolution.
record.source_name: Ron Aharoni, Noga Alon, Eli Berger, Maria Chudnovsky, Dani Kotlar, Martin Loebl and Ran Ziv, “Fair representation by independent sets”, arXiv:1611.03196 (2016).

record.title: The bounded-degree monochromatic density conjecture
record.statement:
Let $\bar d(G)$ denote the upper density of the vertex set of a graph $G$ embedded in $K_\NN$. **Bounded-degree density conjecture.** For every $\Delta\in\NN$, there exists $c>0$ such that for every infinite graph $G$ with maximum degree at most $\Delta$ and every $2$-coloring of $K_\NN$, there is a monochromatic copy of $G$ with

$$
\bar d(G)\geq c.
$$

This is the proposed infinite analogue of the finite bounded-degree embedding theorem of Chvátal, Rödl, Szemerédi, and Trotter; it asks for a uniform positive density depending only on the maximum-degree bound.
record.source_name: Louis DeBiasio and Paul McKenney, “Density of monochromatic infinite subgraphs”, arXiv:1611.05423 (2018).

record.title: Finite-level and nonexistence conjecture for rational newforms
record.statement: For each even weight $k$ and level $N$, let $Q_k(N)$ be the set of quadratic-twist classes of classical newforms with rational coefficients and no complex multiplication, represented at minimal level $N$. **Finite-level and nonexistence conjecture.** For $6\leq k\leq 50$, there is a largest $N_k$ such that $|Q_k(N_k)|\geq 1$; for $18\leq k\leq 50$, this $N_k$ is one of $30$, $10$, $6$, or $2$, as reported in the paper's table; and for $k\geq 52$, there are no non-CM newforms with rational coefficients at all. This is an explicitly computationally motivated expectation based on the displayed table, and the supplied text gives no proof or resolution status.

record.title: Aharoni–Zerbib's extremal ratio conjecture for generalized matchings
record.statement:
For $m<k$, let $\mathcal H(k,m)$ be the family of hypergraphs $H^{(m)}$ arising from $k$-uniform hypergraphs, and define

$$
g(k,m)=\max\{\tau(J)\mid J\in\mathcal H(k,m),\ \nu(J)=1\},\qquad h(k,m)=\sup\left\{\frac{\tau(J)}{\nu(J)}\mid J\in\mathcal H(k,m)\right\}.
$$

Here $\nu$ and $\tau$ denote matching and covering numbers.

**Aharoni–Zerbib's extremal ratio conjecture.**

$$
h(k,m)=g(k,m)\quad\text{for all }m\leq k.
$$

If true, the largest covering-to-matching ratio in this class would always be attained by a hypergraph with matching number one. The source gives no resolution status.
record.source_name: Ron Aharoni and Shira Zerbib, “A generalization of Tuza's conjecture”, arXiv:1611.07497 (2019).
record.references:

record.title: The strong connectedness conjecture for twelve-sphere configurations
record.statement: Let $\operatorname{Conf}(12)[r]$ denote the configuration space of $12$ labeled equal spheres of radius $r$ touching a central unit sphere. **Strong connectedness conjecture.** The radius $r=1$ is the largest radius value at which $\operatorname{Conf}(12)[r]$ is connected. This strengthens the connectedness conjecture at $r=1$ and is supported in the paper by the apparent restriction of the $M_6$ move to $r\leq 1$ and by the criticality of $r=1$; no proof is given.

record.title: Generation conjecture for divisor multiplication operators on the Fock space
record.statement: Let $\mathcal{F}_{\mathcal{A}_n}\cong \mathcal{F}_{[\mathbb{C}^2/\mathbb{Z}_{n+1}]}$ be the common Fock space, and let $D_0,\ldots,D_n$ be a basis of divisors. For each divisor, let $M_{D_i}$ denote the corresponding multiplication operator on $\mathcal{F}$, and let $m>0$ denote the degree sector under consideration. **Generation conjecture.** The joint eigenspaces for the operators $M_{D_i}$, $0\leq i\leq n$, are $1$-dimensional for all $m>0$. This conjecture would allow the divisor multiplication operators to determine multiplication by arbitrary classes, thereby extending the known equivalences of three-point functions with divisor insertions to general $r$-point functions via the degeneration formula.

record.title: Monotonicity of the number of functions determined by additive relations
record.statement:
Let $E$ be a set and $S$ a set of arithmetic functions. For positive integers $k$ and $ell$, let $n(E,S,k)$ denote the number of functions in $S$ determined by the relation

$$
f(a_1+a_2+\dotsb+a_k)=f(a_1)+f(a_2)+\dotsb+f(a_k)
$$

for arbitrary $a_i\in E$. **The monotonicity conjecture for $n(E,S,k)$.** If $E$ and $S$ determine $n(E,S,k)$ in this way, then

$$
n(E,S,k)\ge n(E,S,\ell)
$$

when $k\le \ell$. The paper describes this as a generalization of the preceding conjecture, and gives no resolution.

record.title: Dimension conjecture for secant varieties of cubic Gaussian moment varieties
record.statement:
Let $\mathcal{G}_{n,3}$ be the Gaussian moment variety of order $3$ in $n$ variables, and let $\operatorname{Sec}_k(\mathcal{G}_{n,3})$ denote its $k$-th secant variety. For $K$ defined so that $K+1$ is the smallest integer for which the displayed expression exceeds the ambient dimension $\binom{n+3}{3}-1$, **dimension conjecture for cubic Gaussian moment varieties.** For any $n\geq 2$ and $k\geq 1$, with $k=1,2,\ldots,K$, one has

$$
\dim\operatorname{Sec}_k(\mathcal{G}_{n,3})=\frac{1}{6}k\left[k^2-3(n+4)k+3n(n+6)+23\right]-(n+2).
$$

This conjecture is based on computations of higher secant varieties and extends the proven low-dimensional results; its general validity remains open.
record.source_name: Carlos Améndola, Kristian Ranestad and Bernd Sturmfels, “Algebraic Identifiability of Gaussian Mixtures”, arXiv:1612.01129 (2017).

record.title: Monotonicity conjecture for the degree-coloring index
record.statement:
Let $\tau(G)$ be the smallest number of colors in a degree-coloring of a multigraph $G$. A real-valued function $\kappa(G)$ on multigraphs is **monotone** if, for every multigraph $G$ and every submultigraph $H\subseteq G$, one has $\kappa(H)\leq\kappa(G)$.

**Degree-coloring index monotonicity conjecture.** The degree-coloring index $\tau(G)$ is a monotone function on multigraphs; equivalently, for every multigraph $G$ and every submultigraph $H\subseteq G$,

$$
\tau(H)\leq\tau(G).
$$

The claim concerns whether degree-coloring complexity cannot increase when passing to a submultigraph. The source gives no evidence of resolution.
record.source_name: Mark K. Goldberg, “On degree-colorings of multigraphs”, arXiv:1612.08306 (2016).

record.title: Boundary strict-maximum conjecture for second derivatives of the Fokker–Planck semigroup
record.statement:
Let $h>0$, let $S_N(t)$ be the semigroup in the paper, and let $u_0$ satisfy the conditions of Theorem~. Write $N_0$ for the threshold appearing there. **Boundary strict-maximum conjecture.** For every $t>0$ and $N>N_0$, the endpoint values of the second derivative are strictly smaller in absolute value than its supremum norm:

$$
|(S_N(t)u_0)”(-h)|<\|(S_N(t)u_0)”\|_\infty\quad\text{and}\quad |(S_N(t)u_0)”(1+h)|<\|(S_N(t)u_0)”\|_\infty.
$$

The conjecture is intended to prevent the second derivative from attaining its maximum at the boundary, supporting improved semigroup bounds and hence sharper Fokker–Planck approximation rates.
record.source_name: Dávid Kunszenti-Kovács, “On the error of Fokker-Planck approximations of some one-step density dependent processes”, arXiv:1612.08829 (2016).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1612.08829

record.title: Boundary-layer decay conjecture for second derivatives of the Fokker–Planck semigroup
record.statement:
Let $h>0$, let $S_N(t)$ be the semigroup in the paper, and let $u_0$ satisfy the conditions of Theorem~. Let $N_0$ be the threshold appearing there. **Boundary-layer decay conjecture.** For every $\tau>0$, there exists a constant $K'$ such that, for every $t\in[0,\tau]$ and $N>N_0$,

$$
\max_{z\in[-h,0]\cup[1,1+h]} |(S_N(t)u_0)”(z)|\leq \frac{K'}{N}.
$$

This strengthens the preceding boundary strict-maximum claim by predicting quantitative $N^{-1}$ smallness throughout neighborhoods of the two boundary intervals, potentially yielding sharper approximation bounds.
record.source_name: Dávid Kunszenti-Kovács, “On the error of Fokker-Planck approximations of some one-step density dependent processes”, arXiv:1612.08829 (2016).

record.title: Partition conjecture for graphs with no holes of length at least five
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph with no holes of length at least $5$. A **partition conjecture** asserts that $V(G)$ can be partitioned into two sets, neither of which contains a maximum clique of $G$.

This conjecture would imply the bound $chi(G) leq 2^{omega(G)}$ for graphs with no holes of length at least $5$. Hoang and McDiarmid conjectured that the same partition property holds for all odd-hole-free graphs; the status of the stated conjecture is not established in the supplied text.
record.source_name: Vaidy Sivaraman, “Some problems on induced subgraphs”, arXiv:1612.09349 (2016).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1612.09349

Status: **open** according to the source (as of December 2016).

record.title: A positive lower bound for the scalar curvature of non-flat Ricci shrinkers
record.statement:
Let $n\geq 4$ be a positive integer, and let $(M,p,g,f)$ be a Ricci shrinker. Denote its scalar curvature by $R$, and write $\sup_{x\in M}R(x)$ for its supremum. **Uniform scalar-curvature lower-bound conjecture.** There exists a constant $\epsilon=\epsilon(n)>0$ such that, for every non-flat Ricci shrinker $(M,p,g,f)$,

$$
\sup_{x\in M}R(x)\geq\epsilon.
$$

This conjecture asserts a dimension-dependent gap away from zero for the maximum scalar curvature of non-flat Ricci shrinkers. The supplied text gives no resolution.
record.source_name: Yu Li and Bing Wang, “The Rigidity of Ricci shrinkers of dimension four”, arXiv:1701.01989 (2017).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1701.01989

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2017).

record.title: The conjecture on tritangent planes to tropical sextic curves
record.statement: Let $\Gamma$ be a tropical sextic curve of genus $4$ in $\mathbb{R}^3$. Two tritangent planes to $\Gamma$ are **equivalent** when they determine equivalent tangency divisors on $\Gamma$. **Tritangent-plane conjecture.** Every tropical sextic curve of genus $4$ in $\mathbb{R}^3$ has exactly $15$ equivalence classes of tritangent planes. The preceding theorem proves the upper bound of $15$, and proves equality when the tropical curve is the tropicalization of a sextic on a smooth quadric in $\mathbb{P}^3$; the conjecture asserts equality without that algebraizability hypothesis.
record.source_name: Corey Harris and Yoav Len, “Tritangent planes to space sextics: the algebraic and tropical stories”, arXiv:1701.02353 (2017).

record.title: Balanced dumbbell conjecture for the minimum sum-Balaban index
record.statement:
A **dumbbell graph** $D_{a,b,a'}$ consists of two cliques of sizes $a$ and $a'$ joined by a path with $b$ vertices, so that $a+b+a'=n$. The **sum-Balaban index** is denoted by ${\rm SJ}(D)$. 

**Balanced dumbbell conjecture.** Among all dumbbell graphs $D_{a,b,a'}$ on at least $14$ vertices, the minimum value of sum-Balaban index is achieved for one with $a'=a$ or $a'=a+1$.

The restriction to at least $14$ vertices is motivated by the fact that $D_{2,7,4}$ has the lowest sum-Balaban index among dumbbell graphs on $13$ vertices. The conjecture formalizes the expectation that an optimal dumbbell graph is balanced.
record.source_name: Martin Knor, Jaka Kranjc, Riste Škrekovski and Aleksandra Tepeh, “On the minimum value of sum-Balaban index”, arXiv:1701.02716 (2017).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1701.02716

Status: **open** according to the source (as of January 2017). “For further recent topics and open problems in chemical graph theory an interested reader is referred to .”

record.title: The degree bound for the regular number of connected graphs
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a connected graph. Write $reg(G)$ for the minimum number of edge-partition classes whose induced subgraphs are regular, and let $\Delta(G)$ be the maximum degree of $G$.

**The degree-bound conjecture.** For every connected graph $G$,

$$
reg(G)\leq \Delta(G).
$$

The paper states that this conjecture is false: counterexamples exist, and deciding whether $reg(G)=\Delta(G)+1$ is NP-complete for connected graphs.
record.source_name: Arash Ahadi, Ali Dehghan and Mohsen Mollahajiaghaei, “Algorithmic Complexity of Weakly Semiregular Partitioning and the Representation Number”, arXiv:1701.05934 (2017).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1701.05934

Status: **open** according to the source (as of January 2017). “A summary of results and open problems on edge-partition problems are shown in Table 1.”

record.title: Dickson-image conjecture for the $k=n$ term when $m=n+1$
record.statement: Let $S=\mathbb{F}_q[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$, let $Q=S/(x_1^{q^m},\ldots,x_n^{q^m})$, and let $G=Gl_n(\mathbb{F}_q)$. Assume $m=n+1$ and consider the $k=n$ term of the conjectured Hilbert series for $Q^G$. An invariant polynomial of $Q$ is an **image of an invariant polynomial in $S$** if it is obtained from an element of $S^G$ under the quotient map $S\to Q$. **Dickson-image conjecture.** For arbitrary $n$ and $m=n+1$, one can find invariant polynomials corresponding to the $k=n$ term that are images of invariant polynomials in $S$. This predicts that the relevant graded piece is represented by reductions of Dickson invariants; the source provides no general construction or proof.
record.source_name: Pallav Goyal, “Invariant Theory of finite general linear groups modulo Frobenius powers”, arXiv:1701.06329 (2017).

record.title: The eventual fractional-defect conjecture for connected 4-regular graphs
record.statement:
A graph $G$ is $4$-regular if every vertex has degree $4$. For a graph $G$, let $D(G,2)$ denote the minimum defect in a fractional $2$-coloring. The exceptional graphs are the compositions $C_m[2K_1]$ of odd cycles with the independent graph on two vertices. **Eventual fractional-defect conjecture for connected $4$-regular graphs.** Apart from $G=C_m[2K_1]$ where $m$ is odd, it holds that

$$
D(G)<2
$$

for all but finitely many connected $4$-regular graphs.

Lovász's result gives the general upper bound $D(G,2)\le 2$ for $4$-regular graphs. The exceptional odd-cycle compositions attain $D(G,2)=2$, while computational searches support strict inequality for many other graphs; the conjecture asserts that only finitely many connected exceptions remain beyond those compositions.
record.source_name: Wayne Goddard and Honghai Xu, “Colorings with Fractional Defect”, arXiv:1702.01442 (2019).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1702.01442

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2017).

record.title: Bounded chromatic number for locally bounded tournaments
record.statement:
Let $t\geq 1$. A **t-local tournament** is a tournament $T$ such that, for every vertex $v$, the subtournament induced by the out-neighbors of $v$ has chromatic number at most $t$. The chromatic number $\vec \chi(T)$ is the minimum number of colors in a coloring of $T$ in which every color class is transitive.

**Local-to-global tournament coloring conjecture.** There is a function $f$ such that every $t$-local tournament $T$ satisfies

$$
\vec \chi(T)\leq f(t).
$$

The conjecture was raised in the cited work and was settled for $t=2$; the supplied text also states a theorem proving the same assertion, so its resolution should be checked against the paper's final version.
record.source_name: Ararat Harutyunyan, Tien-Nam Le, Stéphan Thomassé and Hehui Wu, “Coloring tournaments: from local to global”, arXiv:1702.01607 (2017).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1702.01607

Status: the source reports no resolution (as of February 2017); treated as **open**. (An automated reading suggested “solved”, which the source does not establish — worth checking against the literature.)

record.title: Sturmfels's binomial conjecture for the maximum number of Gaussian-mixture modes
record.statement:
Let $m(d,k)$ denote the maximum possible number of modes of a mixture of $k$ Gaussian distributions in dimension $d$.

**Sturmfels's conjecture.** For all integers $d,k\geq 1$, the maximum number of modes is

$$
m(d,k)=\binom{d+k-1}{d}.
$$

This conjecture was proposed in the context of the maximum-number-of-modes problem after the known result $m(d,2)=d+1$. The source does not provide evidence here that the conjecture has been resolved, so its status is recorded as open.
record.source_name: Carlos Améndola, Alexander Engström and Christian Haase, “Maximum Number of Modes of Gaussian Mixtures”, arXiv:1702.05066 (2019).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1702.05066

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of February 2017). “This configuration gives 4 modes for a small window of parameters, disproving the conjecture.”

record.title: The eventual non-$\ell$-distance-balance conjecture for generalized Petersen graphs
record.statement:
Let $GP(n,k)$ be the generalized Petersen graph, let $d$ denote graph distance, and let $D$ be its diameter. For an integer $k\geq 2$, define

$$
n_k=\begin{cases}11,&k=2,\\(k+1)^2,&k\text{ odd},\\k(k+2),&k\geq4\text{ even}.
\end{cases}
$$

**The eventual non-$\ell$-distance-balance conjecture.** For any $n>n_k$, the graph $GP(n,k)$ is not $\ell$-distance-balanced for any integer $\ell$ with $1\leq\ell<D$. Moreover, $n_k$ is the smallest integer with this property. The conjecture formalizes computational evidence that, for each fixed $k$, sufficiently large generalized Petersen graphs are diameter-distance-balanced but fail to be $\ell$-distance-balanced at every smaller distance.
record.source_name: Stefko Miklavic and Primoz Sparl, “-distance-balanced graphs”, arXiv:1702.05257 (2017).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1702.05257

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2017).

record.title: K-theory conjecture for tensor powers of the Leavitt algebra
record.statement:
For $k\geq 1$, let $L_k$ be the quotient algebra identified in the paper with the tensor power $L(1,3)^{\otimes k}$ of the Leavitt algebra. Let $K_0(L_k)$ and $K_1(L_k)$ denote its K-groups, and let $[L_k]$ denote the class of the free rank-one module. **K-theory conjecture.** For every $k\geq 1$,

$$
K_0(L_k)\cong \mathbb{Z}/2
$$

with generator $[L_k]$, and $K_1(L_k)$ is torsion. This conjectural computation is intended to supply the K-theoretic input needed to determine the Grothendieck ring of the associated idempotent-completed category; the answer is not known in general for tensor powers.
record.source_name: Mikhail Khovanov and Yin Tian, “How to categorify the ring of integers localized at two”, arXiv:1702.07466 (2020).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1702.07466

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2017).

record.title: The truncated theta function has no polynomial-length short generating function
record.statement:
Let $r$ be a positive integer and define the truncated theta function by

$$
\vartheta_{r}(t)=\sum_{n=0}^{2^{r/2}}t^{n^2}.
$$

For a short generating function $f$, let $\operatorname{index}(f)$ be the maximum number of denominator factors in one summand, and let $\ell(f)$ denote its length. **The truncated-theta conjecture.** For every fixed $k\geq 1$, the truncated theta function $\vartheta_{r}(t)$ cannot be written as a short GF of length $\operatorname{poly}(r)$ with $\operatorname{index}(\vartheta_r)\leq k$.
record.source_name: Danny Nguyen and Igor Pak, “Complexity of short generating functions”, arXiv:1702.08660 (2017).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1702.08660

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2017).

record.title: Erdős's smaller subgraphs of minimum degree conjecture
record.statement:
Let $k\geq 2$, let $n\geq k+1$, and define

$$
t_k(n)=(k-1)(n-k+2)+\binom{k-2}{2}.
$$

A graph has minimum degree $k$ if every vertex has at least $k$ neighbors.

**Erdős's conjecture.** For every $k\geq 2$ there exists an $\epsilon_k>0$ such that every graph on $n\geq k+1$ vertices and $t_k(n)+1$ edges contains a subgraph of minimum degree $k$ with at most $(1-\epsilon_k)n$ vertices.

Erdős, Faudree, Rousseau and Schelp proved the corresponding existence result with a smaller saving of order $\sqrt n$, while this paper improves the guaranteed saving to at least $\Omega(n/\log n)$. The conjecture asks for a positive constant proportion of the vertices to be removed, and remains open in the supplied source.
record.source_name: Frank Mousset, Andreas Noever and Nemanja Škorić, “Smaller subgraphs of minimum degree k”, arXiv:1703.00273 (2017).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1703.00273

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2017).

record.title: Kostochka–Nakprasit equitable coloring conjecture for d-degenerate graphs
record.statement:
Let $\Delta$ be an integer, let $d\in\{2,\dotsc,\Delta\}$, and let $G$ be a $d$-degenerate graph with maximum degree at most $\Delta$. An **equitable coloring** is a proper vertex coloring in which the color classes have sizes differing by at most one. **Kostochka–Nakprasit's conjecture.** The graph $G$ admits an equitable $k$-coloring whenever

$$
k\geqslant\frac{\Delta+d+1}{2}.
$$

This generalizes the authors' earlier conjecture for $2$-degenerate graphs and would extend equitable-coloring results known for series-parallel and outerplanar graphs. The source presents it as an open problem; the stated theorem for $K_4$-minor-free graphs does not settle the conjecture for all $d$-degenerate graphs.
record.source_name: Rémi De Joannis de Verclos and Jean-Sébastien Sereni, “Equitable Colorings of K\_4-minor-free Graphs”, arXiv:1703.02250 (2017).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1703.02250

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2017).

record.title: Erdős–Sands–Sauer–Woodrow conjecture for quasi-order multidigraphs
record.statement:
Let $T$ be a complete multidigraph whose arcs are the union of $k$ quasi-orders, and let $\gamma(T)$ denote the minimum size of a dominating set, where a set $S$ is dominating when $N^+(S)=V(T)$. **Erdős–Sands–Sauer–Woodrow conjecture.** For every $k$, there exists an integer $f(k)$ such that

$$
\gamma(T) \leq f(k).
$$

This is a digraph formulation of the question of whether finite edge-coloured tournaments admit bounded-size sets reached by monochromatic paths. The statement was open in general, with the case $k=3$ specifically noted as unresolved; the cited paper proves it.
record.source_name: N. Bousquet, W. Lochet and S. Thomassé, “A proof of the Erdős-Sands-Sauer-Woodrow conjecture”, arXiv:1703.08123 (2017).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1703.08123

Status: **open** according to the source (as of March 2017). “Despite some attention (see , , , , for example) the case $k=3$ was still open in both conjectures.”

record.title: Kløve's generalized formula for permutation-code sphere polynomials
record.statement:
Let $d$ be a positive integer and $x$ a real number. Define the $d\times 2d$ matrix $A_{d,x}=(a_{i,j})$ by

$$
a_{i,j}=\begin{cases}
x,&1\leqslant j\leqslant d+1-i,\\
1,&d+2-i\leqslant j\leqslant d+i,\\
0,&d+i+1\leqslant j\leqslant 2d.
\end{cases}
$$

Let

$$
R_d=\{(\rho_1,\rho_2,\ldots,\rho_d)\mid 1\leqslant\rho_i\leqslant d+i,01\leqslant i\leqslant d,\ \text{and}\ \rho_r\neq\rho_s\text{ for }r\neq s\},
$$

and define

$$
\Omega_d(x)=\sum_{\rho\in R_d}a_{1,\rho_1}a_{2,\rho_2}\cdots a_{d,\rho_d}.
$$

**Kløve's generalized conjecture.** For every positive integer $d$,

$$
\Omega_d(x)=\sum_{m=0}^d{d\choose m}(m+1)^d(x-1)^{d-m}.
$$

Kløve introduced this function to obtain bounds for the sizes of spheres in permutation codes under the Chebychev distance. The original conjecture is the specialization $x=2$; the paper proves this generalized identity, settling the conjecture positively.
record.source_name: Victor J. W. Guo and Yiting Yang, “Proof of a conjecture of Kløve on permutation codes under the Chebychev distance”, arXiv:1704.01295 (2017).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1704.01295

Status: the source reports no resolution (as of April 2017); treated as **open**. (An automated reading suggested “solved”, which the source does not establish — worth checking against the literature.)

record.title: The scout-number conjecture for effective exploration of integer grids
record.statement:
A scout process consists of $c$ scouts moving on $\mathbb{Z}^d$ according to a scout protocol $\mathcal{P}=\langle c,\mathcal{S},x_0,\mathbf{q}_0,\Pi\rangle$. The hitting time of $x\in\mathbb{Z}^d$ is $\inf\{n\geq 0:\exists i\text{ such that }X_n^i=x\}$, and the protocol is **effective** when every grid point has finite mean hitting time. It is known that $d+1$ scouts suffice for every $d\geq 1$.

**The scout-number conjecture.** For $d\geq 3$, any effective scout protocol on $\mathbb{Z}^d$ requires at least $d+1$ scouts.

The claim extends the paper's theorem for $d\in\{1,2\}$ and, together with the known sufficiency of $d+1$ scouts, would identify the exact minimum number of scouts needed for effective exploration of $\mathbb{Z}^d$.
record.source_name: Lihi Cohen, Yuval Emek, Oren Louidor and Jara Uitto, “Exploring an Infinite Space with Finite Memory Scouts”, arXiv:1704.02380 (2017).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1704.02380

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2017).

record.title: The Euler-characteristic lower-bound conjecture for reflexive toric Calabi–Yau cones
record.statement:
Let ${\cal X}$ be a toric Calabi–Yau $n$-fold with toric diagram $\Delta_{n-1}$, let $Y$ be its Sasaki–Einstein base, and let $V(b_i^{*};Y)$ denote the minimum volume. Let $\widetilde{X(\Delta_{n-1})}$ be the completely resolved toric variety associated with $\Delta_{n-1}$, and let $\chi(\widetilde{X(\Delta_{n-1})})$ be its Euler number. **Euler-characteristic lower-bound conjecture.** The minimum volume satisfies

$$
V(b_i^{*};Y)\geq \frac{1}{\chi(\widetilde{X(\Delta_{n-1})})}.
$$

The bound is saturated when ${\cal X}$ is an Abelian orbifold of $\mathbb{C}^{n}$. The claim is motivated by computations for reflexive toric Calabi–Yau $3$-, $4$-, and $5$-folds; its asserted universality for all reflexive toric Calabi–Yau $n$-folds remains open.
record.source_name: Yang-Hui He, Rak-Kyeong Seong and Shing-Tung Yau, “Calabi-Yau Volumes and Reflexive Polytopes”, arXiv:1704.03462 (2017).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1704.03462

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2017).

record.title: Hamid's independent transversal domination bound for connected graphs
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a non-complete connected graph on $n$ vertices. For a graph $G$, an **independent transversal dominating set** is a dominating set $S\subseteq V(G)$ such that $S\cap I\neq\emptyset$ for every maximum independent set $I\in\Omega(G)$; let $\gamma_{it}(G)$ denote the minimum cardinality of such a set. **Hamid's conjecture.**

$$
\gamma_{it}(G)\leq\left\lceil\frac{n}{2}\right\rceil.
$$

The preceding theorem establishes the bound when $\alpha(G)\geq n/2$; the paper states that this conjecture is not true in general.
record.source_name: Hongting Wang, Baoyindureng Wu and Xinhui An, “Independent transversal domination number of a graph”, arXiv:1704.06093 (2017).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1704.06093

record.title: Forest maximum-degree repetition conjecture
record.statement:
Let $F$ be a forest on $n$ vertices, and let $f(F)=f_2(F)$ denote the minimum number of vertices that must be deleted to obtain an induced subgraph with at least two vertices attaining its maximum degree, or with fewer than two vertices. **Forest conjecture.** If

$$
n\leq\frac{t^3+6t^2+17t+12}{6},
$$

then $f(F)\leq t$, and this bound is sharp. This conjecture concerns the extremal value of the deletion parameter for forests; the supplied text does not establish it, so its resolution remains open.
record.source_name: Yair Caro, Josef Lauri and Christina Zarb, “Equating two maximum degrees”, arXiv:1704.08472 (2017).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1704.08472

record.title: Maximum-degree boundedness conjecture for equating degrees
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph and, for $k\geq 2$, let $f_k(G)$ be the minimum number of vertices that must be deleted to obtain an induced subgraph with at least $k$ vertices attaining its maximum degree, or with fewer than $k$ vertices. Define

$$
g(\Delta,k)=\max\{f_k(G):\Delta(G)\leq\Delta\}.
$$

**Bounded-degree conjecture.** For every $k\geq 2$ there is a constant $g(k)$ such that

$$
g(\Delta,k)\leq g(k)\sqrt{\Delta}.
$$

The source states that this conjecture would imply the Caro–Yuster conjecture. It is presented as an unresolved problem, and no proof or disproof is supplied.
record.source_name: Yair Caro, Josef Lauri and Christina Zarb, “Equating two maximum degrees”, arXiv:1704.08472 (2017).

record.title: The sharp constant in the average absolute inner-product inequality
record.statement:
For each dimension $n$ and every $x\in\mathbb{R}^n$, define the average absolute inner product over the sign vectors $v_i\in\{-1,1\}^n$ by

$$
\frac{1}{2^n}\sum_{v_i\in\{-1,1\}^n}|\langle x,v_i\rangle|.
$$
The largest absolute constant $\alpha$ such that this quantity is at least $\alpha\lVert x\rVert_2$ for all $x\in\mathbb{R}^n$ and all dimensions $n$ is conjectured to satisfy

$$
\frac{1}{2^n}\sum_{v_i\in\{-1,1\}^n}|\langle x,v_i\rangle|\geq\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\lVert x\rVert_2,
$$
i.e. $\alpha=1/\sqrt{2}$. This identifies the proposed sharp universal constant in the average problem, which is used to improve the lower bound for the Banach–Mazur distance between the cube and the crosspolytope.
record.source_name: Fei Xue, “On the Banach-Mazur Distance between the Cube and the Crosspolytope”, arXiv:1705.01353 (2017).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1705.01353

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2017).

record.title: Conjecture on the size of the largest critical percolation cluster in a uniform triangulation
record.statement:
Let $T_n$ be a uniform triangulation with $n$ faces, and perform a critical site or bond percolation on $T_n$. For random variables, write $X_n\approx n^{\alpha}$ when, for every $\epsilon>0$, the probability that $n^{\alpha-\epsilon}<X_n<n^{\alpha+\epsilon}$ tends to $1$ as $n$ tends to infinity. **Largest-cluster conjecture.** If $\mathfrak{C}_{\mathrm{max}}$ denotes the largest black cluster in the percolated triangulation, then

$$
\mathrm{v}(\mathfrak{C}_{\mathrm{max}})\approx n^{7/8}.
$$

The prediction follows the heuristic that a critical cluster of size $n$ is contained in a triangulation of size of order $n^{8/7}$; it further asserts that the initial cluster has a positive chance of being the largest cluster after the filling operation. The claim remains conjectural.
record.source_name: Olivier Bernardi, Nicolas Curien and Grégory Miermont, “A Boltzmann approach to percolation on random triangulations”, arXiv:1705.04064 (2017).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1705.04064

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2017).
